interaction_contract.sequence_navigation: manual previous/next, optional explicit play only after route gates pass
interaction_contract.scope: Only declared scope parts are visible; unrelated specimens hidden. Reset all overrides when leaving sequence.
interaction_contract.snapshot_resolution: visible_parts is complete within scope; unspecified scope parts hidden; highlight_parts always visible; unknown selectors fail validation.
interaction_contract.display_labels: Resolve aliases by exact legacy selector; do not replace stored selector identity.
interaction_contract.fluid_spaces: Use labelled low-opacity fluid/space cues, not opaque tissue fills.
interaction_contract.motion: No global pulsing, rotation or breathing used as a substitute for mechanism. No mesh morphs between stages.
interaction_contract.external_card: Prefix denotes explanatory non-mesh node, never a part selector.
interaction_contract.support_status: No baseline animation sidecar exists. This data requires a viewer adapter for automatic application; snapshots remain manually usable.

scale_contract.pelvis: 1 model unit = 100 mm; representative organ anatomy
scale_contract.limitations: Inherited teaching scales, not measured patient morphometry; detached specimens are not literal adjacent structures or a universal ruler.

sequences.title: Follicle organisation and endocrine cycle
sequences.mechanism: Compartment-specific steroidogenesis couples follicular state to endometrial state.

steps.title: Read the reserve and growing follicles
steps.caption: Compare stages; activation and early growth precede the final cyclic antral cohort. The surface covering does not generate these oocytes.

steps.title: Antral cohort and dominant follicle
steps.caption: Compare growing antral follicles with atresia. This specimen places representative stages together; it is not a time-lapse of one ovarian section.

steps.title: Separate the two steroidogenic populations
steps.caption: LH supports thecal androgen production; FSH supports granulosa aromatase conversion to estrogens. Use labelled signal arrows and a conversion card, not luminal flow.

steps.title: LH surge and the oocyte–cumulus complex
steps.caption: Sustained preovulatory estradiol permits positive feedback and the LH surge. Oocyte meiotic resumption and follicular changes precede release. No rupture deformation is supplied.

steps.title: Released secondary oocyte
steps.caption: Switch to the separate enlarged specimen: the released secondary oocyte has its zona and surrounding cumulus/corona cells. The detached specimen is not physically beside the ovary in the pelvis.

aggregate_fallback.notice: Zona selector covers the complete comparison row; highlighted stage is the current teaching target.

steps.title: Postovulatory corpus luteum
steps.caption: The postovulatory follicular tissue becomes an endocrine corpus luteum. Progesterone acts on the estrogen-primed endometrium; compare the secretory endometrial inset separately.

steps.title: No-pregnancy branch
steps.caption: Without pregnancy support, luteal function declines and ovarian steroids fall. Follow the separate endometrial breakdown sequence. Scar formation is not a sudden geometric substitution.

steps.title: Pregnancy-support branch
steps.caption: Implanting trophoblast supplies hCG support to the corpus luteum. The corresponding conceptus belongs to a separate developmental scale and stage.

schematic_limitations: Comparative stage field; no same-cycle primordial-to-preovulatory time-lapse.
Hormone levels are qualitative; no mandatory 28-day cycle, fixed ovulation day, paired ovary alternation or concentration curve.
Oocytes, zona and corona selectors aggregate instances; single-follicle isolation requires an authored instance manifest.
Antrum is fluid; the zona is acellular, corona/cumulus are cell populations; do not animate antral fluid as another tissue shell.
acceptance_checks: The highlighted oocyte, zona, corona and cumulus attachment remain distinguishable in contextual view.
Endocrine arrows cannot be mistaken for vessels or luminal transport.
Pregnancy and no-pregnancy branches remain mutually exclusive teaching outcomes.

sequences.title: Tubal pickup, transport and fertilisation
scope_parts: Mucosa of uterine tube (lamina propria folds)
sequences.mechanism: Epithelial surface function, muscular activity and tubal fluid support gamete and embryo transport through an open tube.

steps.title: Open pickup relationship
steps.caption: The ovary releases into the peritoneal environment near the fimbriae. The open ostium admits the oocyte–cumulus complex; no sealed ovary-to-tube conduit is represented.

steps.title: Ampullary fold, epithelium and common lumen
visible_parts: Mucosa of uterine tube (lamina propria folds)
highlight_parts: Mucosa of uterine tube (lamina propria folds)
steps.caption: Read connective-tissue fold cores covered by one epithelial surface facing a common lumen. Fold branches are not independent ducts.

steps.title: Three transport contributors
visible_parts: Mucosa of uterine tube (lamina propria folds)
steps.caption: Show a representative ciliary effective-stroke direction toward the uterus; distinguish muscle contractility and tubal secretions as additional contributors.

steps.title: Sperm ascent is a separate route
steps.caption: Trace a selected sperm-ascent route toward the tube. This arrow indicates anatomical passage and not passive reverse ciliary transport, survival probability or clinical patency.

steps.title: Ampullary fertilisation
steps.caption: Fertilisation usually occurs in the ampulla. Use the enlarged gamete comparison; sperm have their own exaggerated scale. Molecular interaction is explained rather than a ZP3-only lock-and-key animation.

aggregate_fallback.notice: Zona selector covers the complete comparison row; highlighted stage is the current teaching target.

steps.title: Embryo transport toward the uterine cavity
steps.caption: Follow the uterine-directed route while opening the separate cleavage-stage sequence. Marker motion is teaching transport only, with no measured speed or tube transit timing.

schematic_limitations: No fixed rate, ciliary frequency, flow fraction or fertilisation success.
Do not turn a transverse ampullary section into evidence of its whole longitudinal path.
A lumen marker is gated on a builder-supplied saved-output path; part highlights work without such a path.
Representative secretory cells are not individually identifiable in the baseline smooth epithelial selector; cell detail must be supplied before cell-specific motion.
acceptance_checks: Common lumen and core-versus-epithelium organisation remain legible.
Oocyte pickup does not imply fused tube/ovary tissue.
Sperm ascent and uterine-directed embryo transport carry separate legends.

sequences.title: Fertilisation, cleavage and implantation bridge
sequences.mechanism: Sequential developmental states separate fertilisation, cavity formation, zona exit, implantation and bilaminar differentiation.

steps.title: Secondary oocyte before fertilisation
steps.caption: Compare the secondary oocyte with its acellular zona and cellular corona. Acrosome-dependent sperm passage and membrane fusion are described without unsupported receptor certainty.

aggregate_fallback.notice: Zona selector covers the complete comparison row; highlighted stage is the current teaching target.

steps.title: Pronuclear zygote
steps.caption: After fertilisation-related oocyte activation and completion of meiosis II, two pronuclei are present. They do not remain as two separate nuclei through all cleavage stages.

aggregate_fallback.notice: Zona selector covers the complete comparison row; highlighted stage is the current teaching target.

steps.title: Early cleavage
steps.caption: Read successive cleavage comparisons, not three embryos produced by one zygote. Cell partitions increase while early overall size remains constrained by the zona.

aggregate_fallback.notice: Zona selector covers the complete comparison row; highlighted stage is the current teaching target.

steps.title: Compaction and morula
steps.caption: Compaction and a solid multicellular morula precede a fluid-containing blastocyst. The represented cell count is schematic.

aggregate_fallback.notice: Zona selector covers the complete comparison row; highlighted stage is the current teaching target.

steps.title: Pre-hatching blastocyst
steps.caption: Identify outer trophoblast, one-sided inner cell mass and fluid blastocoel. Pale cavity fill is a space cue, not tissue.

aggregate_fallback.notice: Zona selector covers the complete comparison row; highlighted stage is the current teaching target.

steps.title: Hatching bridge
steps.caption: Before attachment, the blastocyst emerges from the zona. The baseline row supplies no hatching aperture or intermediate mesh; this is an explanatory card, not a demonstrated rupture.

steps.title: Initial attachment and invasion bridge
steps.caption: Approximate first-week/second-week transition: attachment at the uterine epithelial surface is followed by trophoblast invasion. The later implanted inset must not appear in this step as if it were initial attachment.

steps.title: Later second-week implanted conceptus
steps.caption: Now show the existing later bilaminar inset, source-designed at approximately post-fertilisation day 12–13: epiblast faces amniotic cavity, hypoblast faces yolk-sac side, and the connecting stalk spans toward chorionic tissue.

steps.title: What happens later is not shown
steps.caption: Week-three gastrulation produces definitive embryonic germ layers from epiblast-derived cells. Hypoblast is not simply the embryo's definitive endoderm. No primitive-streak mesh is supplied.

schematic_limitations: Intervals are approximate post-fertilisation age, not cycle day or clinical gestational age.
No mesh morphing, exact cell-count claim or measured embryo size from display.
Shared early-embryo zona selector spans stages; a pre-hatching blastocyst-specific zona must come from an instance manifest or remain a caption.
Initial attachment/hatching are text bridges until independent intermediate geometry is authored and reviewed.
acceptance_checks: No layer label equates hypoblast with definitive embryonic endoderm.
Next/back cannot bypass both hatching and initial-attachment explanations.
Bilaminar and pre-hatching stages have persistent stage banners.
Fluid spaces have distinct legend and opacity from cell populations.

sequences.title: Endometrium, secretion, breakdown and implantation
sequences.mechanism: Hormone-dependent tissue state changes affect glandular secretion, stromal organisation and local breakdown or pregnancy support.

steps.title: Read the secretory tissue architecture
steps.caption: Follow one gland from its epithelial opening through its lumen into the basal region, surrounded by supporting stroma. The represented glands are examples, not full coverage.
steps.geometry_notice: Hiding the implanted conceptus does not restore nonpregnant geometry: its authored implantation recess remains. This is a tissue-detail reference from the implanted specimen.

steps.title: Arterial supply is separate from gland secretion
steps.caption: Compare the arterial routes supplying functional and basal regions. Gland secretion goes toward gland lumen and surface; blood does not travel through gland lumens.
steps.geometry_notice: Hiding the implanted conceptus does not restore nonpregnant geometry: its authored implantation recess remains. This is a tissue-detail reference from the implanted specimen.

steps.title: Proliferative comparison card
steps.caption: After menstrual loss, retained basal tissue supports regeneration under estrogen. The displayed coiled secretory glands are reference geometry, not a proliferative-phase reconstruction.
steps.geometry_notice: Hiding the implanted conceptus does not restore nonpregnant geometry: its authored implantation recess remains. This is a tissue-detail reference from the implanted specimen.

steps.title: Secretory preparation
steps.caption: Progesterone following ovulation changes glandular secretion and stromal state. This inset shows a representative secretory pattern; do not infer a biopsy date from schematic gland shape.
steps.geometry_notice: Hiding the implanted conceptus does not restore nonpregnant geometry: its authored implantation recess remains. This is a tissue-detail reference from the implanted specimen.

steps.title: Nonpregnant progesterone-withdrawal branch
steps.caption: Local proteolytic and inflammatory processes contribute to functional-layer breakdown following progesterone withdrawal. Vasoconstriction alone is not the complete explanation. Basal tissue remains.
steps.geometry_notice: Hiding the implanted conceptus does not restore nonpregnant geometry: its authored implantation recess remains. This is a tissue-detail reference from the implanted specimen.

steps.title: Menstrual outflow route
steps.caption: Trace anatomical outflow from uterine cavity through the cervical canal and vagina. This is a route comparison, not a rendered volume, clot formation or whole-layer synchronous shedding.

steps.title: Pregnant implantation branch
steps.caption: Alternatively, show the later second-week implanted conceptus in locally altered maternal tissue. Trophoblast/endometrial interactions and gland-associated support precede mature placental circulation; that circulation is not supplied.

schematic_limitations: Only secretory/implanted geometry is supplied; other tissue-phase shapes are explanatory cards.
The presence of a later conceptus changes this to a pregnant decidual context; it is not a normal nonpregnant secretory biopsy.
Straight vessels are not declared wholly insensitive to hormones; retention of basal tissue is a regional outcome.
No detailed spiral-artery remodelling, lacunar perfusion or mature placental circulation animation without new reviewed anatomy.
acceptance_checks: Gland epithelium, lumen and stroma remain visually separable.
Artery and gland arrow styles differ and do not cross compartments improperly.
Menstrual and pregnancy branches are clearly exclusive.
Functional shedding is described as local breakdown, not entire block disappearance.

sequences.title: Milk synthesis, ejection and drainage
sequences.mechanism: Alveolar epithelial secretion is distinct from myoepithelial ejection and branching duct transport.

steps.title: Declare lactation teaching state
steps.caption: This sequence teaches established lactation in a representative section. Lobules contain secretory units; fat and fascia are supporting context. Architecture is not calibrated lactating-human morphometry.

steps.title: Milk synthesis by secretory epithelium
steps.caption: Prolactin supports synthesis by alveolar epithelial cells into the alveolar lumen. This cellular function is a labelled detail card because the gross lobule mesh does not identify each alveolar cell.

steps.title: Milk ejection is a different event
steps.caption: Suckling-related sensory signalling can elicit oxytocin release; myoepithelial contraction moves milk from secretory lumens into ducts. Neural/pituitary and myoepithelial anatomy are explanatory callouts, not existing separate meshes.

steps.title: Trace the drainage route
steps.caption: Follow the chosen terminal unit through branching ducts toward its nipple outlet. Historical sinus labels denote subareolar segments; do not show sac reservoirs filling and emptying.

steps.title: Milk removal and continued secretion
steps.caption: Removal of milk helps sustain production; synthesis and ejection remain separate. Do not infer output or feeding adequacy from anatomical lobe count.

schematic_limitations: Established lactation function card uses representative architecture; no universal lobule/duct count, milk capacity or output.
No sac-like sinus-storage animation. Preserve the historical selector as an alias to subareolar segments.
Myoepithelial cells, detailed alveolar lumens, pituitary and sensory nerves are not existing individually selectable parts.
Axillary node markers are not a complete lymphatic route and do not receive milk-flow arrows.
acceptance_checks: A selected terminal route is continuous at saved-output junctions and ends at a nipple opening.
Outer duct tissue cannot masquerade as a verified lumen path.
No flow overlays start before native and export route inspection.
Breast skin removals are labelled cut surfaces, not natural perforations.

sequences.title: Independent pelvic routes at the artery–ureter crossing
sequences.mechanism: Independent urinary and arterial routes pass close to cervical structures without forming a shared junction.

steps.title: Trace the ureter toward bladder
steps.caption: Follow the ureter toward the bladder; keep cervical context visible. Bilateral geometry needs an instance manifest for true unilateral focus.

steps.title: Trace the uterine arterial supply
steps.caption: Highlight the arterial route toward the uterus independently of the ureter. No intersystem fluid exchange is implied.

steps.title: Pause at the crossing
steps.caption: Show the local crossover with unobstructed cervical context. Separation varies between individuals and positions; this representative model gives no surgical safe distance.

schematic_limitations: Local relationship teaching only; incomplete fascial, neural and vascular context.
Combined bilateral part names cannot prove left/right tracking or exact distance.
No simulated clamping, dissection or injury.
acceptance_checks: The two highlighted systems remain separate at the crossing.
Context makes the relationship to cervix and bladder understandable.
Do not display patient-safe distances from model coordinates.

route_contracts.optional_motion_requirement: Selected unilateral actual-lumen centerline manifest; direction legend explicitly sperm ascent; no timing or fertilisation probability.
Selected unilateral actual-lumen centerline, lumen containment and junction checks; stop at uterine cavity, never continuous motion into bilaminar conceptus.
Saved-output lumen continuity and outlet anchors; route marker is schematic, not calibrated fluid or shed-volume simulation.

Per-terminal-unit lumen route and true nipple outlet, authored branch ids, expected junctions, saved-output continuity, native/export inspection; no large sinus-sac retention. The terminal alveolar lumen detail must exist before animation claims secretion into it.

integration.application_path: Lead emits sidecar alongside refined cache; viewer/manual teaching resolves exact final selectors, display aliases and each step snapshot. No shared application edit by specialist.
integration.native_adapter: Not implemented or claimed; lead must declare unsupported automatic playback if final native consumer is unavailable.
integration.path_manifest: Builder supplies named source-frame route anchors and segment/branch ids; transform them with exactly the same warp/export frame as their parent tissue. Do not infer centerlines from detached part positions.
gate_order: Resolve all part identities against final manifest.
Verify relevant saved-output path continuity and lumen containment.
Inspect native and exported candidate route in the same named teaching view.
Enable optional motion only for reviewed routes; otherwise retain captions and ordered highlights.

sources.title: Reed and Carr: The Normal Menstrual Cycle and the Control of Ovulation
sources.fetch_scope: Full teaching chapter opened, 686 extracted lines
sources.relevance: Two-cell steroidogenic relationship, LH surge, luteal/endometrial coupling; qualitative phases rather than patient hormone curves.

sources.title: Duke Histology: Female Reproductive System
sources.relevance: Follicle, tubal fold, cervical and endometrial tissue context. Some ovarian material is monkey; no human dimensional calibration.

sources.title: Raidt et al.: Ciliary function and motor protein composition of human fallopian tubes (2015)
sources.relevance: Coordinated ciliary flow toward uterine cavity. Five healthy FT donors; retrospective PCD observations do not quantify universal transport contributions.

sources.title: Patrat et al.: Zona pellucida from fertilised human oocytes induces a voltage-dependent calcium influx and the acrosome reaction in spermatozoa, but cannot be penetrated by sperm (2006)
sources.fetch_scope: PubMed abstract opened, 486 extracted page lines
sources.relevance: Human zona interactions require species-aware qualification; avoid mouse-derived ZP3-only certainty. Research results do not establish a universal molecular animation.

sources.title: ZP domain of human zona pellucida glycoprotein-1 binds to human spermatozoa and induces acrosomal exocytosis (2010)
sources.relevance: Additional human zona components participate experimentally; do not teach a single ZP3 receptor as the complete mechanism.

sources.title: UNSW Embryology: Implantation
sources.relevance: Hatching/attachment/invasion bridge; bilaminar/extraembryonic cavities are later than the pre-hatching row. Approximate stages, not a measured timeline.

sources.title: UNSW Embryology: Gastrulation
sources.relevance: Epiblast origin of definitive three embryonic germ layers in week three; avoid hypoblast-to-definitive-endoderm equivalence.

sources.title: Salamonsen et al.: Production of endometrial matrix metalloproteinases, but not their tissue inhibitors, is modulated by progesterone withdrawal in an in vitro model for menstruation (1997)
sources.relevance: Progesterone withdrawal shifts proteolytic balance in a culture model; menstrual breakdown cannot be taught solely as spiral-artery vasoconstriction.

sources.title: Marbaix et al.: Menstrual breakdown of human endometrium can be mimicked in vitro and is selectively and reversibly blocked by inhibitors of matrix metalloproteinases (1996)
sources.relevance: Evidence for MMP-dependent tissue breakdown in explant model; not an in vivo menstrual perfusion simulation.

sources.title: WHO: Infant and Young Child Feeding, The physiological basis of breastfeeding
sources.relevance: Alveolar milk synthesis, myoepithelial ejection, neural/pituitary reflex and duct drainage; production versus ejection.

sources.title: Ramsay et al.: Anatomy of the lactating human breast redefined with ultrasound imaging (2005)
sources.relevance: Branching subareolar ducts; no classical sac-like sinus in 21 lactating participants. Do not extend that result to all physiologic states or universal dimensions.

sources.title: Magrina et al.: Does a Uterine Manipulator Increase the Distance of the Ureter to the Cervix and/or Vagina? An Anatomical Cadaver Study (2022)
sources.kind: institutional record of primary cadaver study
sources.relevance: Ureter/uterine artery crossing near cervical/vaginal context; variable separation in 22 fresh-frozen pelvises; no universal safe distance.

sources.title: Gross and Histologic Anatomy of the Pelvic Ureter: Clinical Applications to Pelvic Surgery (2019)
sources.relevance: Pelvic ureter route and uterine artery crossover as local clinical teaching context; avoid complete nerve or surgical exposure claims.
